**What this is.** This workbook summarizes past work on finding each donor's teosinte alleles (H_d) on chr10 from the pooled BC1 samples of
pool 1B, from the first joint CRISP run on 2026-09-17 to the discovery procedure recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` on 2026-09-23. It covers the
CRISP settings, our step-4 post-filter, the B73 controls, the reference-range set, joint versus per-donor discovery, the BC2S3 artificial pool
used as the required witness, and founder versions v1 to v5. It does not cover the PHG imputation and painting details; they appear here only
as agreement numbers. Every number comes from the files named in each section's "Sources" line.

::: {.callout-note}
## Outcome (what holds on 2026-09-23)

- **Discovery is per donor.** CRISP runs on **the donor's BC1 samples + its BC2S3 artificial pool only**, on the lowcopy BED, with
  `-p 12 --sm 0 --mmq 20 --filterreads 0 --minc 2`. The **witness veto** then keeps records with ≥ 1 ALT read in the BC2S3 pool. The
  **two B73 pools** (NCBI ERR3288215 and the B73 check pool skim10) are counted at the kept sites with `bcftools mpileup` and enter at
  **step 4** as the zero class. The script is **`PHG/bin/donor_discovery_chr10.sbatch`** (`docs/DECISIONS.md`, 2026-09-23, correcting
  the row entered earlier that day).
- **Step 4** (`PHG/bin/pilot_step4_postfilter_llr.py`) computes a pooled LLR on the 1/12 lattice and assigns tiers A / B / C / ref.
  Founder alleles need ALT reads in more than one of the donor's BC1 samples (decided 2026-09-19).
- **Reference ranges = lowcopy** (gene ± 500 bp ∪ non-TE intergenic): 8,095 ranges and 26.0 Mb on chr10. Fixed 1 Mb and 250 kb bins were
  rejected on 2026-09-21 because they gave a false HET background outside introgressions.
- **Founders per donor:** tier A (v5 on Zd.0040_P1: 48,791 alleles) and A+B (v4: 103,809 alleles). The RTIGER poolseq lane uses the
  **tier-A sites** with rigidity 500 (decided 2026-09-21), and PHG B uses the A+B founder.
- The B73 controls had **no measurable effect** on allele quality or imputation. What they add is a veto list of about 1,500 sites and about
  5% more alleles.
:::

## 1. Starting point: joint CRISP on the 12 pool-1B samples (09-17)

Each BC1 sample is one library made from 6 pooled BC1 plants. That gives 12 haplotype copies per locus, a teosinte allele fraction of j/12
(mean 0.25, never > 0.5), and a poolseq model with CRISP `-p 12`. Diploid genotype callers were dropped for BC1, so only allele counts are
taken from BC1 reads. Pool 1B holds 12 samples from 6 donors: Zx.0100_P4 (S_1B_1, 2), Zx.0150_P2 (3, 5), Zx.0130_P1 (4), Zd.0040_P1
(6, 8, 10), Zl.0010_P1 (7, 9, 11) and Zd.0010_P3 (12). The CRAMs were made with minibwa `-x sr` and MAPQ ≥ 20, and reach 14–18x over gene
space.

The first discovery ran all 12 pools together on the chr10 gene BED (2,239 intervals, 15.3 Mb) with `-p 12 --filterreads 0 --minc 2`
(job 870569). It took 30:41 wall time and 411 MB, and produced **412,488 records / 351,437 biallelic SNPs**. That result was identical to
the `--minc 4` run. CRISP's quality-test threshold (QV p-value −5.0) already needs about 3 alt reads at Q30, so `--minc` below 3 does not
bind. The setting that controls 2-read sites is `--qvpval` (≈ −3.5), which was not run (user decision). Other CRISP facts found here:
`LowDepth` is a label and does not discard records (93–99% of records carry it at 14–18x), and CRISP exits 1 on success.

A resource test with 384 columns (12 CRAMs × 32, chr10:20–30 Mb gene space) took 1 h 36 min wall time, 4.08 GB peak RSS and 1 core. That
is about 1.6 CPU-h per 10 Mb of gene space.

Sources: `agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md` (Inputs; Step 2 --minc 2; 384-column test); `agent/handover_20260918_195309.md` §1;
`docs/DECISIONS.md` (2026-09-1x row).

## 2. Step 4: our post-filter on CRISP output

Step 4 is our own post-processing, not part of the CRISP protocol (the user stressed this on 2026-09-21). The same applies to the tiers,
the LLR, the zero class and the witness veto. The script is `PHG/bin/pilot_step4_postfilter_llr.py`. For each biallelic SNP record and each
pool it takes the depth n_i (ref + alt reads, ADf+ADr+ADb) and the alt count a_i.

- **Likelihood on the 1/12 lattice.** Under H1, the number of carriers among the 6 plants is j_i ~ Binom(6, 1/2). The allele fraction is
  f_j = j/12 and p_j = f_j(1−eps) + (1−f_j)eps, so L1_i = Σ_j w_j Binom(a_i | n_i, p_j). Under H0, L0_i = Binom(a_i | n_i, eps).
  LLR_d is the sum over the donor's pools of log L1_i − log L0_i.
- **eps_site from a zero class.** The error rate at a site comes from pools of donors that are confidently non-carriers (LLR < −3 at
  eps0) when those pools hold ≥ 20 reads. Otherwise eps0 = 0.005 is used and the site is flagged `no_zero_class`. With `--extra-counts`,
  pools counted outside CRISP (the B73 controls, via `mpileup_ad_counts.py`) are added as pools for each record.
- **Flags:** `hidepth` (summed depth > 2× median), `af_gt_half` (donor alt fraction > 0.5, binomial p < 0.01), `inconsistent` (one pool
  has a ≥ 3 while another pool has n ≥ 10 and a = 0), `single_sample`.
- **Tiers:** **A** = LLR ≥ 6.9, ≥ 2 pools with alt and no flags. **B** = LLR ≥ 4.6 and no hidepth/af flags. **C** = LLR ≥ 2.2.
  **ref** = LLR ≤ −4 and n ≥ 12.

On the joint set (job 870612, minc-4 set, which is identical to minc 2), the tiers separated cleanly against the taxon assemblies. Tier A
matched the assembly at 49–60% and tier B at about 30%:

| donor | samples | tier A | A in assembly | tier B | B in assembly | tier C | confident REF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Zd.0040_P1 (Gigi) | 3 | 30,892 | 59.5% | 97,442 | 30.5% | 14,336 | 181,201 |
| Zx.0100_P4 (TIL18) | 2 | 58,643 | 51.5% | 48,250 | 29.6% | 10,570 | 196,835 |
| Zx.0150_P2 (TIL18) | 2 | 62,288 | 48.6% | 42,809 | 30.2% | 8,694 | 186,550 |
| Zl.0010_P1 (no assembly) | 3 | 117,609 | – | 37,076 | – | 6,806 | 161,511 |
| Zx.0130_P1 | 1 | 0 | – | 61,900 | 43% | 11,399 | 515 |
| Zd.0010_P3 | 1 | 0 | – | 72,449 | 54% | 13,026 | 781 |

Tier A requires alt reads in ≥ 2 pools, so donors with a single sample get no tier-A sites.

**The > 1-pool rule (09-19).** A per-site allele test used pileups of three ALT-rich Zd.0040_P1 lines, the B73 check and the B73 skim pool.
It measured the REF fraction inside RTIGER ALT blocks: 0.15 for tier A and 0.49 for tier B. By the number of pools carrying the alt allele
it was 0.13 for 3 pools, 0.44 for 2 pools and 0.49 for 1 pool. Roughly one third of the 128,302 A+B founder alleles were positions where
the lines carry the B73 base. Most of these were tier-B alleles supported by only 1–2 of the 3 samples. The decision taken was that a
founder allele needs alt reads in more than one of the donor's BC1 samples.

One finer split was recorded as data but not adopted as a rule: 2-pool alleles whose silent pool had ≥ 10 reads were contradicted at 0.49,
versus 0.19–0.21 when the silent pool had < 10 reads.

Sources: `PHG/bin/pilot_step4_postfilter_llr.py` (docstring); `agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md` (Step 4 debug; 09-18 late per-site

## 3. Reference ranges: gene ± 500 → lowcopy; fixed bins rejected

- **Gene ranges (09-17/18).** Discovery and founder reference blocks first covered only gene space. The first 3-founder graph (B73 +
  taxon + donor) gave the donor a haplotype in 2,517 of 4,685 chr10 ranges. The intergenic ranges only offered B73 or the taxon founder,
  which caused the dosage under-call (ALT → HET) and fragmentation. On 09-18 the graph was restricted to gene ranges (2,489) with two
  founders (B73 + H_d) and the taxon founder dropped.
- **Non-repeat test (09-19).** CRISP was run on the TE complement (9,838 ranges, 20.7 Mb) and gave 705,973 SNP records. Contradiction
  fractions for Zd.0040_P1 strict alleles were: genic low-copy 56,665 alleles at 0.33, intergenic low-copy 92,251 at 0.37, and the genic
  TE part 17,864 at 0.41. Masking TE out of genic space therefore buys no precision, while the intergenic low-copy space adds alleles of
  about the same quality.
- **Lowcopy (09-20).** Gene ± 500 bp ∪ low-copy intergenic (the TE complement of the MaizeGDB TE GFF), merged across ≤ 200 bp gaps and
  kept if ≥ 500 bp (`PHG/bin/make_union_bed.py`). On chr10 this gives **8,095 ranges, 26.0 Mb, median 1.4 kb**. The joint-discovery
  founder under the > 1-pool rule grew to 166,789 alleles for Zd.0040_P1 and 140,365 for Zx.0100_P4.
- **Fixed bins rejected (09-21).** PHG was also run with 1 Mb and 250 kb bins on Zd.0040_P1. The fixed bins put a false HET background
  outside introgressions, so lowcopy stays as the range set. For context, reads per line × range at tier-A sites had a median of 1 on
  lowcopy (54% zero), 49 on 250 kb bins and 233 on 1 Mb bins. The known cost of lowcopy is a dosage under-call in ranges with few reads.

![Local copy: Zd.0040_P1 chr10, RTIGER vs PHG on 1 Mb bins, 250 kb bins and lowcopy ranges (stay 0.99).](../../agent/pilot_1B_chr10_results_v10/Zd0040_RTIGER_PHG1Mb_PHG250kb_PHGlowcopy_s099.png)

Sources: `agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md` (Attempt 5; 09-18 evening; 09-19 01:42; 09-20 20:17); `agent/handover_20260921_025746.md`
(Decisions 1); `docs/DECISIONS.md` (2026-09-20, 2026-09-21); `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`; `agent/handover_20260921_155429_simulation_benchmark.md`

## 4. Joint versus per-donor discovery, and the B73 controls

On 2026-09-18 the user decided to rerun discovery **per donor**, with each run taking only that donor's samples. The trade-off noted at
the time was that CRISP's contingency test needs pools without the allele, and a single donor's samples all carry nearly all of H_d. The
CRISP README also requires ≥ 2 pools, so the 1-sample donors cannot run alone. Two B73 control pools were therefore prepared:

- **ERR3288215** (ENA, ~20x raw, 2×150 NextSeq, labelled WGA). It was aligned in job 886211 (3 h 21 min, 48 GB) to
  `results/b73_control/ERR3288215/B73_ERR3288215.cram`, which reaches **15.5x** genome-wide after `-F 0x904 -q 20`.
- **skim10**: 10 clean B73 skim checks merged (PN5_SID468 and PN3_SID236 dropped) into `results/b73_control/skim10/B73_skim10.bam`. It has
  97.6 M reads and 5.72x genome-wide, with one RG added via `addreplacerg`.

**Per-donor CRISP with the B73 pools (Zd.0040_P1, union BED, job 896958).** The pools were S_1B_6/8/10 + ERR3288215 + skim10, all `-p 12`.
The run took 15 min and 350 MB and gave 451,807 SNP candidates. With B73 as the zero class in step 4, Zd.0040_P1 had tier A 70,139 and
tier B 221,635, compared with 60,440 and 193,793 from joint discovery on the union set. The founder (> 1 pool) had 174,768 alleles versus
166,789.

**What the B73 pools measured:**

- Alt reads at 0.17% (ERR3288215) and 0.38% (skim10) of bases.
- 19,303 candidates with any B73 alt read. Treating B73 as a "donor" gave tiers A 143 / B 579 / C 827, which is the veto list.
- Across 797k candidates, B73 was clean at 788,210 sites. There were 8,510 sites with a single alt read, 563 mismap-like sites and 7 fixed
  divergent sites.
- NIL background alt reads inside RTIGER REF blocks were 1.9% at B73-alt sites versus 1.0% elsewhere. B73 self-mismapping is therefore a
  minor source of false alleles.
- The per-site test of founder v3 gave 0.33 / 0.38 / 0.42 (genic low-copy / intergenic low-copy / genic TE), the same as the
  joint-discovery founder. Imputation was also unchanged (87.2% introgressed, 99.9% clean, B73 check 0 bins).
- Conclusion recorded at the time: the B73 zero class does not change allele quality or the painting. What it adds is a veto list of about
  1,500 sites and about 5% more alleles.
- 2,615 of the 174,725 founder-v3 alleles (1.5%) sit on B73-flagged sites and were not vetoed in v6/v7.

## 5. The BC2S3 artificial pool as required witness (09-21)

The artificial pool is the 38 Zd.0040_P1 BC2S3 BAMs merged on chr10 into one read group (29.3 M reads). It entered CRISP as a sixth pool
next to the 3 BC1 samples and 2 B73 pools, on the union BED with `-p 12` (job 898439). The run took 17.5 min and gave **425,431 records**.

The **witness veto** (`PHG/bin/veto_witness.py`, formerly `filter_bc2s3pool.py` on hazel) keeps records with ≥ 1 ALT read in the witness
pool (ADf+ADr+ADb alt). It kept **240,745 and dropped 184,686 (43%)**. Step 4 then ran with the B73 zero class, and the BC2S3 pool was
mapped as its own "donor" rather than pooled into the donor likelihood. That gave 162,803 tier A/B sites, of which 103,837 had alt in > 1
BC1 pool. The resulting **founder v4** had **103,809 alleles**.

With the BC2S3 pool present, CRISP already has ≥ 2 pools, so the B73 pools are no longer needed for that purpose.

Sources: `agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md` (09-21 00:44); `PHG/bin/veto_witness.py`; `agent/handover_20260920_221920.md` (item 10);
`agent/handover_20260921_025746.md` (Decisions 2); `docs/PLAN_production_genotyping_poolseq.md` §1.2–1.4.

## 7. Tier A sites for the RTIGER poolseq lane (decision 09-21)

RTIGER (nilhmm `rtiger`, design BC2S3) was first run on the 174,725 founder-v3 sites. With the default rrate of 0.01 it gave 325 segments
per line. Rigidity 250 (RTIGER's r = 5 on the 50K set × the 47× marker density) gave 10 segments per line, and rigidity 500 gave 3.

The user decided on 09-20 to exclude sites with zero ALT reads across the donor's BC2S3 lines, which is the rule the 50K data use. It
removed 44% of the sites (76,864 of 174,725). The user corrected an earlier reading that this made things "worse": that referred only to
agreement with PHG. The filter in fact reduces fragmentation (median 3 → 2 segments per line) and shifts HET → ALT.

**DECISION (user, 2026-09-21 01:50):** the poolseq RTIGER lane uses **tier A sites**. These are sites with LLR ≥ 6.9, alt in > 1 of the
donor's BC1 samples, no inconsistency flag, and the BC2S3 pool as witness, with zero-ALT-across-lines sites excluded. The caller is nilhmm
`rtiger`, design BC2S3, rigidity 500. The user called this "the sweet spot for RTIGER". On Zd.0040_P1 it gives 44,757 variable tier-A sites
and median 2 segments per line (max 14). PHG keeps the A+B founder (v4).

The plan of record generalizes the rigidity as R_c = 5 × n_sites_c / n_50K_sites_c, which is 500 on chr10 for ~45k sites versus 3,695.

## 8. Discovery procedure of record (2026-09-23) and the scripts

`docs/DECISIONS.md` has two rows dated 2026-09-23. The first put the 2 B73 control pools inside CRISP, together with the donor's BC1
samples and the BC2S3 pool. The second row **corrects** it and is the one that holds. **CRISP = the donor's BC1 samples + its BC2S3 pool
only.** The B73 comparison happens in step 4 (zero class), using ERR3288215 and skim10 counted at the vetoed sites. The pilot uses the
current check pool, and the publication-ready pipeline must build the check pool itself.

**`PHG/bin/donor_discovery_chr10.sbatch`** implements this (commit 3d0f6c5) in five steps:

1. Build the BC2S3 artificial pool: all the donor's lines on chr10 (B73 checks excluded), merged, one RG.
2. Run CRISP on the BC1 samples + the BC2S3 pool, on the lowcopy BED, with `-p 12 --sm 0 --mmq 20 --filterreads 0 --minc 2`.
3. Apply the witness veto (`veto_witness.py`).
4. Count the two B73 pools at the kept sites with `bcftools mpileup -q 20 -Q 20 -a AD` → `mpileup_ad_counts.py`.
5. Run step 4 with the B73 counts passed via `--extra-counts`; the BC2S3 pool is its own "donor".

The script runs as a short-QOS job (2 h, 8 CPU, 48 GB).

**`PHG/bin/discovery_perdonor.sbatch`** is the earlier parameterization of the same v4 steps. It uses the MAPQ20-realigned BC2S3 CRAMs as
the witness, and its header puts **the 2 B73 pools inside CRISP** ("zero class for eps_site in step 4"). Its Zx.0100_P4 run (job 932554)
therefore predates the 2026-09-23 decision and does not follow it. That run gave 345,952 records. The veto kept 79,119 (23%), and step 4
gave tier A 40,434 / B 17,253 / C 6,391 / ref 1,399 (numbers as given in the request for this workbook; the job log is not among the local
sources).

**Almost no REF calls in the step-4 table.** The witness veto runs before step 4 and keeps only records with an ALT read in the donor's
own BC2S3 lines. Those are sites where the donor's material shows the allele, so few of them can reach ref (LLR ≤ −4, n ≥ 12) for the
donor. The job-932554 table has 1,399 ref, whereas the joint run without a veto had 181,201 confident REF for Zd.0040_P1 and 196,835 for
Zx.0100_P4. Those REF sites came from other donors' variants.

Sources: `docs/DECISIONS.md` (both 2026-09-23 discovery rows); `PHG/bin/donor_discovery_chr10.sbatch` (header); `PHG/bin/discovery_perdonor.sbatch`
